cards.heading: Definition
cards.question: What is the LLM-maintained wiki pattern?
cards.answer: An LLM incrementally builds and maintains a persistent wiki as its knowledge substrate — writing and revising pages as material arrives — instead of retrieving over raw documents each session.

cards.heading: Write-time distillation
cards.question: What is the core mechanism behind the LLM-maintained wiki pattern?
cards.answer: It moves the work to write time: the model distils incoming material into named, linked pages and revises them as understanding changes, so future sessions read consolidated pages instead of re-deriving from raw sources.

cards.heading: Contrast with RAG
cards.question: How does the LLM-maintained wiki pattern differ from retrieval-augmented generation?
cards.answer: RAG searches unprocessed source documents at query time, so nothing accumulates; the wiki pattern distills material into revisable pages at write time, so knowledge compounds.

cards.heading: Legibility advantage
cards.question: What advantage does a maintained wiki have over an embedding index?
cards.answer: It is human-legible and correctable — a person can inspect and fix a page — unlike an embedding index.

cards.heading: Trade-off accepted
cards.question: What cost does the wiki pattern accept in exchange for compounding knowledge?
cards.answer: Maintenance cost and the risk of distillation errors, traded for persistence, legibility, and curation.
